controls.description: Automated identity-driven provisioning: 'When Workday records a hire, transfer, or termination, Okta picks it up within the hour. design_questions: Who owns and approves the Okta group rules mapping Workday job profiles to the NetSuite baseline roles (employee centre, expense entry)? Is that approval documented?

notes: Proposal for human review only; it makes no conclusion on whether any control is effective. Four controls (LHP-01 to LHP-04) were identified for NetSuite and ClaimsLens across AC-PROV, AC-UAR and CM-CHG. The client policy ('policy') states several criteria that differ from the Finance Systems narrative ('narrative'). These are recorded as contradictions for the engagement team to resolve: approver for access (narrative L13 vs policy L5), UAR reviewer (narrative L17 vs policy L7), UAR removal timeframe (five business days, narrative L17, vs ten business days of the review, policy L7), and develop/deploy segregation (narrative L21 vs policy L9). Design findings for the team to consider: (a) no completion timeframe is stated for the semi-annual NetSuite access review; narrative L17 and policy L7 state only a frequency, so actual export and sign-off dates are reported without a pass/fail threshold; (b) no ClaimsLens role or permission mapping is stated (narrative L11 refers only to 'NetSuite and ClaimsLens accounts'), so ClaimsLens/AC-PROV is shown as partially covered; the LHP-01 PROV-D criterion covers NetSuite baseline roles only; (c) the Finance Systems Manager develops, approves and deploys NetSuite changes (narrative L21), so self-approved changes are reported separately, and the team decides whether they are exceptions; (d) the Okta administration path (manual group-membership, group-rule and application-assignment changes) can grant NetSuite or ClaimsLens access outside Workday events and Jira requests, and is not covered by any described control. Coverage gaps the team should weigh: (1) No user access review is described for ClaimsLens, Okta, AWS or GitHub. (2) No provisioning control is described for ClaimsLens access beyond Okta-created accounts, or for Cirrus Ops access to AWS, the database or GitHub. (3) Cirrus Ops builds and operates ClaimsLens, and the narrative states 'Cirrus Ops does not provide a SOC report' (narrative L25). Any reliance on Cirrus Ops-performed activities therefore needs direct testing or another basis. (4) NetSuite 'went live on 1 October 2025' (narrative L7).
